Overview and relationship to the market

Probit Offset Boosted is a 5-member bagged ensemble and a standard published architecture, not the production model. Every figure below is read from a declared artifact: this report fits nothing, loads no booster, recomputes no prediction and calls no betting optimiser.

Evaluated races

Probit Offset Boosted is better than the market by 0.005054 race_multinomial_log_loss on the evaluated races. The direction holds in every one of the 11 evaluated years.

This market-anchored booster learns its own utilities directly under the multinomial-probit likelihood; it is not a link-only reuse of a Softmax fit.

How each evaluation year was fitted

These are walk-forward figures rather than one model's: the model is refitted for each evaluation year on the seasons before it, so the result concatenates 11 separately fitted models and no evaluation year's outcomes appear in its own fit. This run did not record the year its training window starts, so this report does not name one.

Deltas in this report use model_minus_market_log_loss: race_multinomial_log_loss, where negative is better. That is stated because three delta fields existed in this repository and they did not all point the same way.

Similarity is not accuracy

Similarity is not accuracy. Correlation, rank agreement, top-choice agreement, probability mass moved, divergence and entropy describe how the model relates to the market; paired race log-loss says which probabilities better described the recorded winners.

What this report covers

Every metric here is reported beside the market's own implied probabilities on the same races, normalised within each race. The delta is this model's race log loss minus the market's on the same races.

Every figure in this report covers the evaluation window beginning in 2016. 2015 is earlier than the window and is excluded from every evaluation figure below, including the bankroll paths. The feature-effect grid is the one exception, and says so where it appears: a learned response direction is a property of each year's fit rather than of the evaluation population.

Test races

Years

2016-2026
Seeds

Some years are warm-up rather than evaluation

2015 had no earlier year to fit a utility scale on and took the predeclared theoretical value (insufficient_history). The utility is divided by that scale, so those years amplify corrections where a fitted scale halves them, and their stakes and claimed edges are several times any fitted year's. They are excluded from every figure in this report and named here rather than labelled and left in.

Model diagnostics

Link-aware movement

Runners binned by the offset correction — what enters the link — against how far the link moved their probability away from the paired reference, which is the same mean utilities through the softmax link. So the movement isolates the shock distribution and nothing else.

Input bandRunnersMean signed inputMean absolute inputMean probability movementMean absolute movementMean winner loss delta

-0.35 to -0.1522,668-0.2190.219-0.00060.0006+0.015
-0.15 to -0.0523,679-0.0990.099-0.00000.0004+0.001

+0.05 to +0.159,862+0.0880.088+0.00050.0007-0.007
+0.15 to +0.352,648+0.1970.197+0.00110.0011-0.015
+0.35 to +0.7510+0.3630.363+0.00130.0017--

This describes the link's input, not individual feature effects. Feature probability effects require a separate link-aware artifact; inherited utility attribution alone does not supply them. The loss delta is the only column in which being right enters, and it sits beside the movement because a band can move a long way and be no better — negative is better.

Input correction attribution

Not applicable to this model. this architecture fits its own mean under the probit likelihood, so the Offset run's attribution describes a different correction and inheriting it would be the wrong comparison rather than a failed one. Its own attribution exists in principle -- BoostedProbitModel.predict_contrib returns SHAP on this exact correction. This generation has no derived own-fit feature-effects artifact. Use --write-bundles on a future fitting run to retain its exact model weights for subsequent attribution; old utilities alone cannot recover the contributions.

5 of 5 seeds favour the candidate, and every seed agrees on the sign. Seed variation can reflect differences in fitted member utilities and fitted scales. It is not by itself an estimate of integration error; that requires a controlled integration-sensitivity comparison.

The fitted utility scale

Fitted minimum
1.6504
Fitted maximum
1.7363
Theory
0.7797
the value theory predicts

The fitted scale sits above the value theory predicts, in every year: 1.650 to 1.736 against 0.780 (the scale the fallback year used, which is the predeclared theoretical value). Theory gets this wrong and the fit is what the report uses -- a scale asserted from theory would divide the utilities by too little, and at that value the market-relative candidate loses instead of winning. A run that took the theoretical value on faith would have reported the wrong sign, which is why the first year -- which has no history and falls back to it -- is excluded from the headline and labelled.

Promotion gates this run's artifacts can check

GateVerdict
1. paired delta is negativepass
2. no year degrades beyond tolerancepass
3. survives nested calibrationpass
4. direction stable across seedspass
5. improvement exceeds integration error 10xpass

Passing every gate here is not promotion. The gates these artifacts cannot check are in the limitations section, and production remains the five-seed Softmax Offset ensemble until they are met.

Historical settlement and bankroll

These are retrospective prices

Every figure in this section is settled against historical result-page odds and official dividends. Those are the prices after the pool closed, so no bet here could have been placed at them and nothing here establishes profitability.

Diagnostic settlement, not model selection

Secondary diagnostic. This suite selects on paired race log loss; betting returns cannot select a model and are not evidence for or against a probit candidate.

Model-assumed simulation

Bankroll outcomes if model probabilities were true

Question answered: If the stored model probabilities were the true win probabilities, what range of cumulative Kelly returns and drawdowns could racing randomness produce at the observed odds?

Fixed stored context: published model view bagged_probit_offset_boosted / historical Win Odds held fixed as the gross-return proxy / observed race chronology / cumulative evaluation range 2016-2026 / fresh opening bankroll at the first retained year, 2016; no bankroll carried from excluded prior years. Changing a control only reveals an already-computed trajectory; the browser performs no simulation or settlement arithmetic.

every race in the standardized evaluation window that the settlement can settle, not the subset this model staked. An unstaked race has multiplier exactly 1 under both policies, so including it changes no terminal figure; excluding it made the race sequence -- and with it the checkpoints and the shared random draws -- a property of the model, which is what stopped two reports' fan charts being comparable.

These are the stored settings for this run. Compare the population digest, seed and checkpoint schedule before comparing simulations across reports.

Model-assumed outcome simulation

Winners are drawn from the fitted probabilities. This isolates wagering variance conditional on the model being exactly right; it is not evidence that the estimated edge exists.

Rebate-aware large-bank limit

A 10% rebate on net losses is applied without an eligibility threshold, contrasted with Kelly with no rebate. This is a scale-free large-bank limit, not an exact finite-bankroll scenario. Minimum-bet rounding is omitted.

Assumptions:
  • Model probabilities are assumed exactly correct.
  • Historical Win Odds are held fixed and used as the gross return proxy.
  • Race opportunities and chronology are as observed.
  • Winners are drawn independently per race from the stored probabilities.
  • The model is not refitted inside a replicate.
  • Model error, drift, market response and regime change are excluded.

Metric definitions
Analytic expected return
Probability-weighted bankroll multipliers compounded through the observed race order.
Median terminal return
Half of simulated paths finish below this cumulative return and half above.
5th-percentile terminal return
Five percent of simulated paths finish at or below it.
Maximum drawdown
Largest peak-to-trough decline, including the opening bankroll as the initial peak.
Percentile bands
Exact cross-replicate quantiles at each stored chart checkpoint.
Model risk is not included

The model is not refitted inside a replicate. Probability error, model drift, market response and regime change are excluded, so these ranges describe outcome variation under the stored model and odds rather than uncertainty that the model will remain correct.

Limitations

Historical result-page odds are not executable prices

Every stake, return and bankroll figure in this report is computed against historical result-page odds and official dividends. Those are not an executable pre-race price: they are the prices after the pool closed, and a bet placed at them could not have been placed. Nothing here establishes profitability. A profitability claim requires a locked model shadow-tested against timestamped pre-race odds snapshots.

Every test year is also development data

Every year through 2026 has been used as development data in this repository: features were searched, architectures compared and thresholds inspected against these same seasons. The chronological split is real, so a test year is genuinely after its training rows, but no test year is unseen. Treat the forward figures as probability progress rather than as a locked out-of-sample result, and do not select a Kelly level or an edge threshold from this reused history. The confirmation step that this run cannot substitute for is a prospective shadow test against archived pre-race price snapshots.

What this report does not establish

  • It measures Probit Offset Boosted against the market on the evaluated races. It is not a cross-model comparison, and nothing in it ranks this model against another published one.
  • The model-assumed simulation excludes model risk by construction. It answers what racing randomness could do if the stored probabilities were exactly right, so it is not evidence that the estimated edge exists.
  • No interval here bounds refit uncertainty, so no figure carries a stated range over the model itself -- a single number is not evidence of precision.
  • Every figure is out of sample in time but in sample in design: the feature set, the hyperparameters and the staking rules were all chosen with these years visible.
  • Nothing here is a shadow test. A profitability claim needs a locked model run forward against timestamped pre-race prices.
Promotion conditions these artifacts cannot check

An interaction diagnostic across predeclared cohorts, reproduction from a clean identified commit, and confirmation on a future prospective period are not derivable from these artifacts. Production remains the five-seed Softmax Offset ensemble until they are met. Passing the gates that are checkable is not promotion.

The settlement's own statement of what it decides

Secondary diagnostic. This suite selects on paired race log loss; betting returns cannot select a model and are not evidence for or against a probit candidate.

How to verify this report

Provenance is not rendered in this document and it is not missing. Three files sit beside this one, and between them they carry everything the retired technical appendix printed:

FileWhat it lets a reader check
run_lock.jsonevery one of the 19 artifacts this report read, by content digest, with the lock digest of the run that produced them, the source commit and its clean-or-dirty state, and the model and config identity
manifest.jsonwhat this report wrote, by digest and byte size, with the rendering mode and the capability verdict for every section
summary.jsonthe model identity, the population identity, the headline metrics, the market-relationship metrics, every settled Kelly path's identity and endpoints, and the simulation policy inventory with its terminal metrics

This report was generated from source commit bb9ab4cc254a, clean. Its metrics are measured on 8265 race keys whose digest is sha256:81e0285f5e0538d8a2293b4fd026ded45a23a454fbbc9204bdced2c90555728d. The published reports are compared on that digest before publication, so the claim that they cover the same races is checked rather than asserted.
